summary: NASA’s Nancy Grace Roman Space Telescope is prepared to launch aboard a SpaceX Falcon Heavy rocket on Aug. 30. In civil space developments, President Trump signed an executive order creating a U.S. Space Academy and presented the Artemis II astronaut crew with the Congressional Space Medal of Honor, while NASA awarded its first prize in Phase 2 of the agency's LunaRecycle Challenge. Commercial launch activity advanced as SpaceX performed a static-fire test of its Starship Super Heavy booster ahead of Flight 14, following the retrieval of a previous Starship vehicle from the Indian Ocean to be shipped back to Texas, while radar satellite operator ICEYE expanded its international footprint by opening three new offices in a single week. In defense space, a new report revealed the U.S. Space Force spent $124 million on commercial data and services over nearly three years, and the service adopted a digital engineering tool for its nuclear command, control, and communications satellite program. Internationally, Finland and Sweden established a partnership to strengthen counter-drone defense capabilities. In planetary science and astronomy, new findings suggest Mercury’s crust has deeper, hotter volcanic origins than previously estimated, while researchers uncovered evidence pointing to the potential discovery of the first starless galaxy. Readers should watch next for SpaceX’s upcoming Flight 14 test of its Starship Super Heavy launch vehicle.
